paragraphs.source_en: A lmustafa, the chosen and the beloved, who was a dawn unto his own day, had waited twelve years in the city of Orphalese for his ship that was to return and bear him back to the isle of his birth.

units.source_en: A lmustafa, the chosen and the beloved, who was a dawn unto his own day, had waited twelve years in the city of Orphalese for his ship that was to return and bear him back to the isle of his birth.

paragraphs.source_en: And in the twelfth year, on the seventh day of Ielool, the month of reaping, he climbed the hill without the city walls and looked seaward; and he beheld his ship coming with the mist.

units.source_en: And in the twelfth year, on the seventh day of Ielool, the month of reaping, he climbed the hill without the city walls and looked seaward; and he beheld his ship coming with the mist.

paragraphs.source_en: Then the gates of his heart were flung open, and his joy flew far over the sea. And he closed his eyes and prayed in the silences of his soul.

units.source_en: Then the gates of his heart were flung open, and his joy flew far over the sea.
And he closed his eyes and prayed in the silences of his soul.

paragraphs.source_en: But as he descended the hill, a sadness came upon him, and he thought in his heart:

units.source_en: But as he descended the hill, a sadness came upon him, and he thought in his heart:

paragraphs.source_en: How shall I go in peace and without sorrow? Nay, not without a wound in the spirit shall I leave this city. Long were the days of pain I have spent within its walls, and long were the nights of aloneness; and who can depart from his pain and his aloneness without regret?

units.source_en: How shall I go in peace and without sorrow?
Nay, not without a wound in the spirit shall I leave this city.
Long were the days of pain I have spent within its walls, and long were the nights of aloneness; and who can depart from his pain and his aloneness without regret?

paragraphs.source_en: Too many fragments of the spirit have I scattered in these streets, and too many are the children of my longing that walk naked among these hills, and I cannot withdraw from them without a burden and an ache.

units.source_en: Too many fragments of the spirit have I scattered in these streets, and too many are the children of my longing that walk naked among these hills, and I cannot withdraw from them without a burden and an ache.

ja.t: りのあちこちに、あまりにも

paragraphs.source_en: It is not a garment I cast off this day, but a skin that I tear with my own hands.

units.source_en: It is not a garment I cast off this day, but a skin that I tear with my own hands.

paragraphs.source_en: Nor is it a thought I leave behind me, but a heart made sweet with hunger and with thirst.

units.source_en: Nor is it a thought I leave behind me, but a heart made sweet with hunger and with thirst.

paragraphs.source_en: For to stay, though the hours burn in the night, is to freeze and crystallize and be bound in a mould.

units.source_en: For to stay, though the hours burn in the night, is to freeze and crystallize and be bound in a mould.

ja.t: とどまることは、たとえ

paragraphs.source_en: A voice cannot carry the tongue and the lips that gave it wings. Alone must it seek the ether.

paragraphs.source_en: Now when he reached the foot of the hill, he turned again towards the sea, and he saw his ship approaching the harbour, and upon her prow the mariners, the men of his own land.

units.source_en: Now when he reached the foot of the hill, he turned again towards the sea, and he saw his ship approaching the harbour, and upon her prow the mariners, the men of his own land.

paragraphs.source_en: How often have you sailed in my dreams. And now you come in my awakening, which is my deeper dream.
